newsitem.title: INDIA: Four die when police fire on crowd in India.
newsitem.headline: Four die when police fire on crowd in India.

text.p: Four people died and three were seriously wounded on Friday when police opened fire to disperse a mob in the western Indian state of Gujarat, the United News of India (UNI) news agency said.
The violence, linked to a wave of tension between Hindu castes, erupted in Keshod town in Gujarat, UNI said.

Police opened fire at a crowd trying to force shopkeepers to pull down their shutters in response to a general strike call by upper caste groups. Lower-caste Hindus organised a similar protest strike on Wednesday.
On July 11 police opened fire on a mob in Bombay in neighbouring Maharashtra state, killing 12 people.
The Bombay unrest was triggered by the desecration of a statue of social activist B.R. Ambedkar, a leader of the lowest of Hindu castes, called Dalits.
Business in Maharashtra was paralysed last Monday during a strike called by low-caste political parties and supporting groups in protest against the desecration.
The violence caused a conflict between low-caste groups and the Hindu nationalist Shiv Sena party government in Maharashtra.
